meta.title: My game collection as code, on Omarchy
meta.description: How I use AI agents to keep Steam games, emulators, PC ports and decomps in an idempotent Ansible repo inside a distrobox, with my own Omarchy launcher.

hero.title: Not everything is work. Even I need to play.
hero.lede: And my idea of relaxing is, of course, turning my game collection into a software project. Steam games, emulators, PC ports, decompilations, fan games and mod packs, all installed, configured and documented by AI agents in one Ansible repository. It runs inside a container, so my Omarchy desktop never sees a single one of their dependencies. On top sits a launcher I wrote, so the whole thing feels like a console.
hero.shotAlt: My games launcher on Omarchy: a fullscreen grid of 52 game covers including Banjo-Kazooie Recompiled, OutRun, the Colin McRae Rally series, Donkey Kong Country and DOOM 3, with category chips and sort buttons on top.
hero.caption: The launcher on my desktop: every game, port and emulator in one grid, whatever it runs on underneath.

clean.title: The host stays clean
clean.lede: Emulators and Windows games drag in 32-bit libraries, Wine builds, AUR packages and runtime versions that fight each other. None of that touches my desktop. It all lives in one Arch Linux distrobox called gaming, Steam included, and the host keeps only what the desktop needs.
clean.alt: Two panels. Without a container: a Host tower buried under a tangle of library blocks with red Conflicts warnings. With distrobox: the same Host clean with a green dot, and next to it an orange gaming container holding the same blocks in tidy rows, with an Ansible recipe labelled Rebuild anytime.
points: Steam runs inside the box, with my library and its Proton prefixes on their own disk
The NVIDIA driver is passed through, and the one 32-bit library edge case is fixed in the launcher, never on the host
The box renders desktop entries; a small host script validates and installs them, and removes the ones for apps that are gone
Saves are mirrored to my NAS and restored on demand, so wiping the box loses nothing

idempotent.title: Idempotent, so I can break it
idempotent.lede: Every emulator, config, patch and mod set is an Ansible role. Running the playbook a second time changes nothing, so I can experiment freely, reset a single emulator's settings, or rebuild the whole box from scratch and get the same machine back.
idempotent.docs: notes in docs/, one per game, port or fix

research.title: AI does the research, and writes it down
research.lede: For every port, recompilation or stubborn Windows game, an agent researched the sources, wrote the Ansible role and left a note with where to get it, how it is set up and what did not work. Steam games have their own compatibility database under Proton, with each local fix backed by a source.

items.title: Emulators
items.text: ES-DE as the frontend, plus standalone shadPS4, Dolphin, PCSX2, DuckStation, Flycast, xemu, RPCS3, PPSSPP, Azahar, Eden, Cemu, Supermodel and RetroArch with its cores.

items.title: Ports, decomps and recomps
items.text: Native builds such as Ship of Harkinian, 2Ship2Harkinian, Starship, SpaghettiKart, Render96ex and Unleashed Recompiled.

items.title: Windows games
items.text: Wine-managed installs and fixes for games like Colin McRae Rally, OutRun 2006 and the Metal Gear Master Collection.

items.title: Mods, reproducibly
items.text: NexusMods mod sets per game, DLC and patch installers for PS3 and Switch, and per-game RPCS3 settings.

menu.title: My own launcher, made for Omarchy
menu.lede: omarchy-games-menu is a Steam-like fullscreen launcher for Omarchy and Hyprland. It reads the desktop entries the gaming repository exports, so a new game shows up by itself, and it puts everything a keybinding away.
menu.alt: Three layers: a Host slab, an orange distrobox container labelled gaming holding Emulators and PC ports with an Ansible recipe, and a Launcher grid of cover art on top.
points: A Rust CLI, ogm, does the scanning, catalog and persistence; a QuickShell overlay draws the grid
Cover art and metadata from SteamGridDB, and new-release checks on GitHub for ports and recomps
Sorted by most played, name, date added or release date; type anywhere to filter
Scales with Hyprland's monitor setting, opens with one key such as Super+G, and games open fullscreen on a dedicated workspace

note.title: Why it is on this site
note.text: Both repositories were written with the same agents and skills as everything else here. They are the clearest example I have of the rule I apply everywhere: if a machine's setup is not code, it is not documented, and if it is not documented, it will break the day you need it.
